assumptions: An empty `advisory` section is legitimate (every check promoted) and is allowed; only a missing or non-array `advisory` throws. An empty `required` throws, as the issue asks.

Single-reader enforcement is a grep-style test (no other file under ts/test contains the manifest file name as a quoted string literal), following the repo's precedent of executable guards over comments.

Callers needing other sections (externalStatuses, rulesetRules, reviews, mergePolicy) read them via readRequiredChecksManifest<T>(), but required/advisory always go through requiredEntries()/advisoryEntries() so the zero-denominator guard applies to every caller.
Testkit row validation also throws when a required/advisory row has no non-empty `check` string; this goes slightly beyond the issue but is the same zero-denominator class.
